classification.difficultyReason: Find equal base angles in the marked isosceles triangle, transfer an angle vertically across the intersection, then calculate y and verify the stated ratio.

content.prompt: Show that angle $y$ is half the size of angle $x$.

spec.description: Triangles ABE and DBC meet at B. A–B–C and E–B–D are straight lines. Matching single ticks identify BD=CD. Includes all vertex labels, four angle arcs and an external 20° label with pointer. Coordinates derive the isosceles triangle from its 20° apex angle.
spec.mathematics: BD=CD; angle BDC=20°; angle AEB=60°; angle BAE=y; angle BCD=x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Since $BD=CD$, the base angles of triangle $DBC$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle DBC=\angle BCD&=\frac{180^{\circ}-20^{\circ}}{2}\\&=80^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=80^{\circ}$. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $\angle ABE=80^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-80^{\circ}\\&=40^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $y=40^{\circ}=\frac{80^{\circ}}{2}=\frac{x}{2}$, as required.
